bracket: [Textbook misprint: the book's own worked solution concludes r = 8, 3 and never rejects r = 8, which is inadmissible — the left-hand side is a permutation of 4 objects taken r at a time, so r ≤ 4 is required (and the right-hand side needs r ≤ 6). Only r = 3 satisfies the original equation. The quadratic itself is correct; the book simply omits the admissibility check on its roots. Worth knowing that NCERT's printed ANSWER KEY does not repeat this slip — where the exercises pose the same question type (Exercise 6.3 Q7), the key gives the admissible root alone.]
